unit: 1 Terms used in nutrition and nutrition-related problems
topic: Terms used in nutrition and nutrition-related problems
outcome: Define diet, balanced diet, metabolism, malnutrition, undernutrition, overnutrition and deficiency disease.
Give sources and functions of high and low biological value proteins.
Give sources and functions of mono-, di- and polysaccharides.
Give sources and functions of fats.
Give sources and functions of vitamins A, C, D, E, K and the B group.
Give sources and functions of calcium, iron, phosphorus, potassium, sodium, fluoride, chloride and iodide.
Give sources and functions of water and NSP / dietary fibre.
Explain sources and uses of food energy.
Describe digestion in the mouth, stomach, duodenum and ileum.
Explain digestive enzymes as catalysts and bile's role in emulsifying fats.
Explain how nutrients are absorbed and the structure of the ileum.
Plan and serve meals for different ages, occupations, cultures and religions.
Plan for pregnancy, allergies, coeliac disease, diabetes, convalescence and vegetarians.
Plan special-occasion meals, snacks and drinks, and use herbs, spices, garnishes and attractive presentation.
Use DRV and RDI terms and nutritional tools.

unit: 5 Composition and value of the main foods in the diet
topic: Composition and value of the main foods in the diet
outcome: Describe the composition and value of dairy, eggs, fish, meat and soya.

unit: 5 Composition and value of the main foods in the diet
topic: Composition and value of the main foods in the diet
outcome: Describe the composition and value of cereals, fruit, vegetables, pulses, nuts, and fats and oils.
Explain conduction, convection, radiation and the principles of the main cooking methods.

subtopic: Why we cook and sensory properties
outcome: Give reasons for cooking and describe flavour, taste and texture.
Explain caramelisation, coagulation, dextrinisation, browning, gelatinisation, rancidity and smoking point.
Cook to keep nutritive value and use food, equipment, fuel and labour economically.
Describe types of convenience food and weigh their advantages and disadvantages.
Explain food additives, packaging types and what labels show and why.

unit: 8 Basic proportions and methods of making
topic: Basic proportions and methods of making
outcome: Use creaming, melting, one-stage, rubbing-in and whisking methods.

unit: 8 Basic proportions and methods of making
topic: Basic proportions and methods of making
outcome: Make shortcrust, flaky and rough puff pastry.

unit: 8 Basic proportions and methods of making
topic: Basic proportions and methods of making
outcome: Make pouring and coating sauces by roux and blended methods, and thin and coating batters.

unit: 8 Basic proportions and methods of making
topic: Basic proportions and methods of making
outcome: Make sweet and savoury yeast products.
Explain air, carbon dioxide and water vapour, and how bicarbonate, baking powder and yeast introduce gas.
Explain the action of enzymes, bacteria, yeasts and moulds.
Describe personal, food and kitchen hygiene, storage, refrigeration and waste disposal.
Explain reasons for preserving and the principles of canning, drying, freezing, chemicals, modified atmosphere and irradiation.
Describe pasteurisation, sterilisation and UHT, evaporated, condensed and dried milk.
Explain how enzymes and bacteria make cheese and yoghurt.
Organise cooking areas, and choose and care for work surfaces, flooring, walls, lighting and ventilation.
Choose, use and care for cookers, microwaves, slow cookers, fridges and freezers.
Choose, use and care for knives, pans and small electrical equipment.
Spot danger areas and apply safety precautions.
Give first aid for burns, scalds, cuts, electric shock, fainting and shock.
